channel.title: The Augusta Press - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Augusta Press (theaugustapress.com)

item.title: Kentucky fires SEC’s longest-tenured coach in Mark Stoops, hires his replacement hours later
item.description: Kentucky fired the Southeastern Conference’s longest-tenured coach, ending Mark Stoops’ tenure in his 13th season with the Wildcats after back-to-back losing records Monday morning.

item.title: Strom Thurmond back in the state championship for the first time since 2005
item.description: Strom Thurmond faces Hampton County in the Class AA state championship after a strong playoff run.

item.title: Lincoln County one win away from state title game
item.description: Lincoln County enters the semifinals unbeaten and heads to Early County with a state championship berth on the line.

item.title: Generator sparks small fire at Augusta National Golf Club
item.description: A small fire at Augusta National Golf Club on Monday morning, caused by a generator spark in a testing area, was quickly contained with no injuries or damage reported, according to Augusta Fire PIO Chiquita Richardson.

item.title: Drones a threat to prison security
item.description: Drones powerful enough to lift a human have become a routine tool for delivering contraband in Georgia prisons.

item.title: Temporary lane closure scheduled on Hardy McManus Road for starting Dec. 3
item.description: Drivers should expect intermittent lane closures on Hardy McManus Road this week as Columbia County and Reeves Construction begin right-of-way clearing.

item.title: Health inspectors pump the brakes at Jim Hudson’s Luxury Cars Inc.
item.description: The health inspection world grades a score below 70 as failing, but, no restaurants, pools or hotels received a failing score.

item.title: Augusta joins in observing World AIDS Day
item.description: The City of Augusta joined communities around the world in observing World AIDS Day on Monday.

item.title: Planning Commission postpones proposed tiny home village
item.description: The Augusta Planning Commission voted to postpone a proposed tiny home village project on Hephzibah-McBean Road.

item.title: Augusta seeks $2.4 million to manage hurricane mulch
item.description: Augusta officials are seeking approval to buy up to $2.4 million in heavy equipment to safety manage and reuse more than one million cubic yards of wood mulch.
